correctness.rationale: For every squarefree binary sextic over C, a vanishing pairing determinant gives a unique dependent triple of root-pair quadratics, the explicit forms Q1,Q2,Q3, and a minimal rational Weierstrass elliptic surface with six simple doubled discriminant roots and hence six I2 fibers. Conversely the published six-I2 normal form yields such a determinant. A basepoint-free quadratic pencil gives a branch-pair-exchanging involution and genus-one quotient; the converse follows from hyperelliptic involution descent. Symmetric descent gives coefficient degree 15; one-branch nonzero-gradient and repeated-root witnesses prove reduced irreducibility. The two-branch witness has nonzero Jacobian minor. All witnesses independently replay under standalone exact-rational Python 3.
correctness.risks: The proof uses the published six-I2 normal-form classification, ordinary elliptic-surface minimal Weierstrass theory, and established generic genus-two reduced-automorphism results. The finite witness tests alone are not proofs of the global statements.

originality.rationale: Ciliberto et al. explicitly leave the six-singular-fibre branch-position hypersurface equation and its genus-two characterization as Question 25. The present theorem supplies the reduced degree-15 binary-sextic equation, an inverse surface reconstruction, birationality and an exact transverse two-branch stratum. Shaska–Völklein establish the classical genus-two elliptic-subcover locus and its invariant description, so those existing results are cited rather than treated as new. No inspected prior source asserts the full six-I2 equivalence, constructive inverse and transverse-stratum claim together. The historical-priority assessment is provisional and particularly sensitive to classical bielliptic invariant theory.
residual_risks: Classical Clebsch–Bolza/Richelot/Humbert invariant literature might contain a coefficient-equivalent degree-15 form, reducing equation novelty even if the elliptic-surface bridge is not explicitly stated.

value.rationale: Determines a geometrically natural hypersurface equation and its moduli meaning for six-I2 rational elliptic surfaces, precisely addressing an explicit open question. A concrete inverse constructs the elliptic surface from the branch sextic. The transverse two-pairing stratum gives useful singular boundary information and distinguishes double constructions; these statements connect elliptic surface geometry, genus-two Jacobian decompositions and binary sextic invariant theory rather than being an arbitrary finite calculation.
value.risks: Part of the genus-two bielliptic interpretation and Humbert equation is classical; interest is in the complete elliptic surface bridge and explicit geometry.
